chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The head of no one is to be kissed, nor his hand, except the hand of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), or whoever is intended to be the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) by it.
ai.seo_question: Who is permitted to have their head or hand kissed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the etiquette of *ta'zir* (kissing the head or hand) by restricting it primarily to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), with the exception of those kissed with the specific intention of honoring the Prophet. This ruling highlights the distinct status of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing their physical honor from general social customs, while also allowing for flexibility when the act serves as a proxy for reverence toward the Messenger.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Rifa’at Bin Musa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Do not kiss the head (forehead) of anyone, nor his hand, except for the hand of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, or the one who intends Rasool-Allah<sup>azwj</sup> by it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Rufa’ah ibn Musa from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
No one’s head or hand is kissed except those of the Messenger of Allah or one who is intended to be for the Messenger of Allah.”
